scenes.narration: Seventeen people. One page. Then an industry. This is the history of Agile, in about three minutes.

scenes.on_screen: Seventeen people. One page. Then an industry. The history of Agile, in about three minutes. Behind the words, six of the film's own scenes play as previews.

scenes.title: It did not begin in 2001
scenes.narration: It did not begin in 2001. Larman and Basili trace iterative development back to the nineteen thirties, to short improvement cycles at Bell Labs. One programmer later recalled doing incremental development as early as 1957. Then, in 1970, came Winston Royce's paper.

sources.claim: Larman and Basili trace iterative and incremental development (IID) back to the 1930s work of Walter Shewhart at Bell Labs.
sources.title: Iterative and Incremental Development: A Brief History

sources.claim: Gerald Weinberg recalled, in a personal communication quoted by Larman and Basili, that his team was doing incremental development as early as 1957 in Los Angeles.
sources.title: Iterative and Incremental Development: A Brief History

sources.claim: Royce recommended that a program developed for the first time be built twice, so that the version delivered to the customer is in effect the second one.
sources.title: Managing the Development of Large Software Systems

scenes.on_screen: 1930s: Short improvement cycles; 1957: Incremental software, as later recalled; 1970: Royce's paper

scenes.title: Blamed for the waterfall

quotes.quote: I believe in this concept, but the implementation described above is risky and invites failure.

scenes.narration: Blamed for the waterfall. Yet of that simple sequence of phases, Royce himself wrote: I believe in this concept, but the implementation described above is risky and invites failure.

sources.claim: In his 1970 paper Winston Royce drew the simple sequence of phases, said he believed in the concept, and then called that implementation risky and failure-prone.
sources.title: Managing the Development of Large Software Systems

scenes.on_screen: “I believe in this concept, but the implementation described above is risky and invites failure.” (Winston Royce, 1970)

scenes.title: The 1990s: lightweight methods
scenes.narration: The nineteen nineties brought lightweight methods. DSDM, in 1994. Scrum, first presented in 1995. Extreme Programming, from 1996. Crystal, 1998. Feature-Driven Development, 1999. Lightweight was a label nobody really liked.
scenes.say: The nineteen nineties brought lightweight methods. D.S.D.M., in 1994. Scrum, first presented in 1995. Extreme Programming, from 1996. Crystal, 1998. Feature-Driven Development, 1999. Lightweight was a label nobody really liked.

sources.claim: In January 1994 sixteen rapid application development practitioners met in the UK, drawing on James Martin's RAD teaching, and their process definition became the Dynamic Systems Development Method (DSDM).
sources.title: Iterative and Incremental Development: A Brief History

sources.claim: Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland say they developed Scrum in the early 1990s and first presented it together at the OOPSLA conference in 1995.
sources.title: The Scrum Guide (2020)

sources.claim: Fowler, who consulted on the Chrysler C3 payroll project, wrote that it was restarted under Kent Beck's lead in 1996 and first brought together the practices that became Extreme Programming.
sources.title: C3

sources.claim: Alistair Cockburn says he designed the Crystal family of methodologies while working at the Central Bank of Norway, where he helped deliver a project in 1998.
sources.title: Dr. Alistair Cockburn (biography)

sources.claim: Feature-Driven Development was published in 1999 as a chapter by Peter Coad and others in Java Modeling in Color with UML.
sources.title: Iterative and Incremental Development: A Brief History

sources.claim: During 2000 the methods were grouped in articles as "Light" or "Lightweight" processes, a name Highsmith says nobody really liked.
sources.title: History: The Agile Manifesto

scenes.source_line: craiglarman.com · scrumguides.org · martinfowler.com · alistaircockburn.com and 1 more
scenes.on_screen: 1994: DSDM; 1995: Scrum; 1996: Extreme Programming; 1998: Crystal; 1999: Feature-Driven Development

scenes.title: Snowbird, Utah, February 2001
scenes.narration: In February 2001, seventeen people met at Snowbird, a ski resort in Utah, looking for common ground.

sources.claim: From 11 to 13 February 2001 seventeen people met at The Lodge at Snowbird ski resort in Utah.
sources.title: History: The Agile Manifesto

sources.claim: The Manifesto carries seventeen names.
sources.title: Manifesto for Agile Software Development

scenes.on_screen: Kent Beck, Mike Beedle, Arie van Bennekum, Alistair Cockburn, Ward Cunningham, Martin Fowler, James Grenning, Jim Highsmith, Andrew Hunt, Ron Jeffries, Jon Kern, Brian Marick, Robert C. Martin, Steve Mellor, Ken Schwaber, Jeff Sutherland, Dave Thomas

scenes.title: They chose a word: agile

quotes.quote: a bigger gathering of organizational anarchists would be hard to find

scenes.caption: “a bigger gathering of organizational anarchists would be hard to find” Jim Highsmith, 2001
scenes.narration: They chose a word: agile, for adaptiveness. Jim Highsmith wrote that a bigger gathering of organizational anarchists would be hard to find.

sources.claim: Fowler wrote that the group considered several names and settled on "agile" because it captured adaptiveness and response to change.
sources.title: Writing The Agile Manifesto

sources.claim: Highsmith described the group as organisational anarchists and the Manifesto as a symbolic result signed by all participants.
sources.title: History: The Agile Manifesto

scenes.on_screen: “a bigger gathering of organizational anarchists would be hard to find” (Jim Highsmith, 2001)

scenes.title: Four values
scenes.narration: The page states four values. Individuals and interactions, over processes and tools. Working software, over comprehensive documentation. Customer collaboration, over contract negotiation. Responding to change, over following a plan.

sources.claim: The Manifesto states four values, each preferring one thing over another.
sources.title: Manifesto for Agile Software Development

scenes.on_screen: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools; Working software over comprehensive documentation; Customer collaboration over contract negotiation; Responding to change over following a plan

scenes.title: Then it spread
scenes.narration: Then it spread. The Agile Alliance formed in late 2001. ScrumMaster courses began in 2002. The first devopsdays was held in 2009. SAFe dates from 2011. The UK government's service manual says digital services must be agile. And since 2020, a United States defence instruction requires iterative methods on its software pathway.
scenes.say: Then it spread. The Agile Alliance formed in late 2001. ScrumMaster courses began in 2002. The first devopsdays was held in 2009. Safe dates from 2011. The UK government's service manual says digital services must be agile. And since 2020, a United States defence instruction requires iterative methods on its software pathway.

sources.claim: In late 2001 the Agile Alliance was formed as a non-profit organisation to further agile methods.
sources.title: Writing The Agile Manifesto

sources.claim: Schwaber wrote that he developed a two-day ScrumMaster course and first ran it at Object Mentor in Chicago in 2002.
sources.title: About Scrum.org

sources.claim: The first devopsdays was held in Ghent, Belgium, in 2009.
sources.title: About devopsdays

sources.claim: Scaled Agile describes Dean Leffingwell's book Agile Software Requirements, published in 2011, as the foundation and first version of the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe).
sources.title: A Decade in SAFe Adaptation: The Scaled Agile Framework, 10 Years Later

sources.claim: The GOV.UK Service Manual says UK government digital services must be built and run with the agile approach.
sources.title: Agile and government services: an introduction

sources.claim: A U.S. Department of Defense instruction effective 2 October 2020 requires software programmes on its software acquisition pathway to use modern iterative methods such as agile or lean.
sources.title: DoD Instruction 5000.87: Operation of the Software Acquisition Pathway

scenes.source_line: martinfowler.com · scrum.org · devopsdays.org · scaledagile.com and 2 more
scenes.on_screen: 2001: The Agile Alliance; 2002: ScrumMaster courses; 2009: DevOps; 2011: SAFe; 2016: UK government; 2020: US Defense

scenes.title: An industry
scenes.small: Members, certifications and people trained: their own figures, not audited.
scenes.narration: It became an industry. The Scrum Alliance describes a community of nearly 1.8 million. Scrum.org counts over 1.2 million certifications. Scaled Agile says more than a million people trained. These are their own figures, not audited.

sources.claim: In its 2025 annual report the Scrum Alliance describes itself as a global community of nearly 1.8 million professionals.
sources.title: Scrum Alliance 2025 Annual Report

sources.claim: Scrum.org's own count page showed over 1,231,400 Professional Scrum certifications held when read in November 2026.
sources.title: Professional Scrum Certification Count

sources.claim: Scaled Agile's own page said, when read in November 2026, that more than 1,000,000 practitioners had been trained in SAFe and more than 20,000 enterprises had adopted it.
sources.title: About Scaled Agile

scenes.on_screen: 1.8 million: Scrum Alliance; 1.2 million: Scrum.org; 1 million: Scaled Agile. Members, certifications and people trained: their own figures, not audited.

scenes.title: Dave Thomas, 2014

quotes.quote: The word “agile” has been subverted to the point where it is effectively meaningless

scenes.narration: In 2014 Dave Thomas, one of the seventeen, wrote: the word agile has been subverted to the point where it is effectively meaningless.

sources.claim: In March 2014 Dave Thomas wrote that the word "agile" had been subverted until it was effectively meaningless, and that the agile community had become an arena for consultants and vendors.
sources.title: Agile is Dead (Long Live Agility)

scenes.on_screen: “The word “agile” has been subverted to the point where it is effectively meaningless” (One of the seventeen authors)

scenes.title: Martin Fowler, 2018

quotes.quote: the Agile Industrial Complex imposing methods upon people, and that to me is an absolute travesty

scenes.narration: Martin Fowler, in 2018, in his words: the Agile Industrial Complex imposing methods upon people, and that to me is an absolute travesty.

sources.claim: In his 2018 keynote at Agile Australia Fowler called it a travesty that an "Agile Industrial Complex" was imposing methods on people.
sources.title: The State of Agile Software in 2018

scenes.on_screen: “the Agile Industrial Complex imposing methods upon people, and that to me is an absolute travesty” (One of the seventeen authors)

scenes.title: Ron Jeffries, 2018

quotes.quote: it breaks my heart to see the ideas we wrote about in the Agile Manifesto used to make developers’ lives worse

scenes.narration: Ron Jeffries, the same year: it breaks my heart to see the ideas we wrote about in the Agile Manifesto used to make developers' lives worse.

sources.claim: In May 2018 Jeffries wrote that it broke his heart to see the Manifesto's ideas used to make developers' lives worse, and that developers should abandon "Agile".
sources.title: Developers Should Abandon Agile

scenes.on_screen: “it breaks my heart to see the ideas we wrote about in the Agile Manifesto used to make developers’ lives worse” (One of the seventeen authors)

scenes.title: Ron Jeffries, in the same post

quotes.quote: the values and principles of the Manifesto for Agile Software Development still offer the best way I know to build software

scenes.narration: But in the same post, Jeffries wrote that the values and principles of the Manifesto for Agile Software Development still offer the best way I know to build software. His quarrel was with the word, not the values.

sources.claim: Jeffries ended by saying the Manifesto's values and principles were still the best way he knew to build software.
sources.title: Developers Should Abandon Agile

scenes.on_screen: “the values and principles of the Manifesto for Agile Software Development still offer the best way I know to build software” (The word, not the values)

scenes.title: Where things stand
scenes.caption: One author says the page will endure.
scenes.narration: Where do things stand? At the end of 2024, the Agile Alliance joined the Project Management Institute. In February 2026, the Manifesto's twenty-fifth anniversary was marked by a retreat on software development in the age of AI. One author, Jon Kern, says the page will endure.
scenes.say: Where do things stand? At the end of 2024, the Agile Alliance joined the Project Management Institute. In February 2026, the Manifesto's twenty-fifth anniversary was marked by a retreat on software development in the age of A.I.. One author, Jon Kern, says the page will endure.

sources.claim: PMI signed an agreement on 31 December 2024 under which the Agile Alliance joined PMI.
sources.title: Agile Alliance Joins Project Management Institute (PMI)
sources.publisher: Project Management Institute (Business Wire release carried by FinancialContent)

sources.claim: Thoughtworks marked the 25th anniversary of the Manifesto with a retreat in Utah from 1 to 3 February 2026 on software development in the age of AI.
sources.title: Thoughtworks marks 25th anniversary of Agile Manifesto with Future of Software Development Retreat

sources.claim: At the 25th anniversary Kern told The Register that the Manifesto would endure because its first value, individuals and interactions, is key.
sources.title: Agile Manifesto turns 25 - just in time for vibe coding to test it
